recipes.name: Quick Pickled Jalapeño Rings
ingredients_raw: 10 large jalapeno peppers, sliced into rings

steps.text: Combine water, vinegar, sugar, kosher salt, garlic, and oregano in a saucepan over high heat. Bring mixture to a boil, stir in jalapeño peppers, and remove from heat.
Pack peppers into two 8-ounce jars using tongs and cover with vinegar brine mixture. Let pickles cool completely at room temperature.
Cover jars with tight-fitting lids and refrigerate until needed.

raw_recipe.headline: Quick Pickled Jalapeño Rings
raw_recipe.description: These pickled jalapeños are quick to make using a pickling mixture of vinegar, sugar, garlic, and oregano for a delicious kick on nachos or sandwiches.

review.reviewBody: Pickled jalapeno rings are one of my most favorite things. I've always wanted to learn how to make them--this recipe made it possible. I added some crushed red pepper, that was the only change I made. I did not add the jalapeno peppers to the saucepan, I went ahead and put them in the canning jar and once the vinegar mixture came to a boil, I poured it over the peppers in the jar, put a lid on it and let it sit like that for ten minutes before refrigerating. I have not used them yet as I want them to sit in the vinegar for a week or two to really get good. I'll update my review once I've had a chance to try them. Five stars for this recipe for just being awesome. I am so tickled I could make my own. VERY easy.

After some mods this turned out perfectly to my taste. Way less sugar (1/4 tsp) to make it more spicy, added 1/2 sliced carrots and onions. Only one whole garlic clove and pulled out after the 10 min. Left serrano peppers whole but did poke holes in top and bottom so the insides could get filled. The oregano was a game changer. It was just like the name brand but more crunchy and less expensive.

Excellent! I love "all things pickled," but usually not a fan of adding sugar, so I used half (1.5 tbsp). I also used fresh oregano, and did not rinse the sliced peppers to keep the seeds in. Super easy and 24 refrigerated hours later, you'll have pickled jalapenos better than any store bought!

Been making these for about a year now...love them! I do use less sugar we like them hot, everything else the same but I double the brine. I do prefer to stuff my jar tight then add the very hot liquid and put tops on fast, as this will seal the jars. Cover the jars with a towel to cool and listen for the pop sealing sound. When sealed they can be put in the cupboard. If any jars do not seal then put in the fridge, and use first.

Too many ingredients. I just use white vinegar, turmeric and jalapenos (getting rid of seeds and membrane.) Just put it in a glass jar, tightly sealed, and pop it in the fridge. Takes about 4-5 days, shaking the jar once a day.

We love this recipe, we grow our own jalapeños and have made this numerous times. I cold pack the jalapeños and pour the brine in the jar over the jalapeños. We let them cool and store in the fridge. We also have added fresh sliced carrots, sliced onion and jalapeños to the jar and cover with the brine recipe. Several people have asked for the recipe! Thank you!

As good as the ones from the store - but I love that I can make them! I used jalapeños that I grew in my garden. 

I made three modifications: I only used 1 tablespoon of sugar, added 1/4 teaspoon of turmeric, and poured the hot liquid over the slices in the jar as other users suggested. I let these sit in the fridge for 36hrs before taste-testing. They are pretty hot!

I don’t boil the rings, I jam them in the sterilized jar and then pour the boiled mixture over them up to 1/2 in from top then cool and refrigerate. Been doing this for years now, and have used them for up to two years at the most. With this method they are a lot crispier.

I have been making this for years. I used to buy pickled jalapenos until I brought home a jar of mushy jalapenos. I make them slightly different, I slice the jalapenos and stuff a jar with them, I boil the mixture in the microwave and pour it over the jalapenos into the jar. I seal the jar and tap the bottom edges to get the bubbles to rise open the jar and top it off. I repeat until no more mixture will fit. I posted a jar I just made and one made several weeks ago. Yummy!

Easy peasy! As others have said, I cut down on the sugar. I made a double recipe for the brine with only 1 tablespoon sugar. I also poured the boiling brine over the prefilled one quart mason jar. Very good!

I don’t eat spicy so I’m not a good judge but my husband loves these! What I love about this recipe is that I can make them as the summer goes along and the peppers ripen. I usually use half jalapeños and half mild banana peppers because that’s what we’re growing and I get 2 thumbs up every time!

This recipe makes way too much liquid for the ratio. I have almost half left over. Have made this recipe many times an I always cut the liquid by a third. I usually make 4 quarts at a time. If you multiply recipe times eight that equals 12 cups of liquid and I always wind up with ahout 4 cups of liquid left over. Now I make only about 8 cups of liquid to make 4 quarts of product.
This recipe is definitely a keeper. I shared it with friends and family. The peppers stay crispy. They taste delicious Pickling some more peppers today. It's a must make!

This is a very easy recipe with great results. I cut the rings thin on a mandolin and rinsed away some of the seeds to keep the heat in check. Other than that, I made the recipe as written. The taste is great; much more flavor and snap than store-bought. I'll make this one again!

These actually keep well for weeks without noticeable change in taste or texture. I keep them on hand at all times to spunk up grocery store salad kits, tuck into sandwiches, minced into tartar sauce with a splash of green Tabasco, quesadillas/burritos/tacos (all Mexican food of course). Almost anything bland is better with pickled jalapenos to the rescue. I like them in mac-n-cheese (with bacon), Costco vegetable barley soup, in grilled cheese sandwiches... This is truly a well-loved staple in our house.
I cut the sugar down to 1 tablespoon.
Have made these sooo many times....the best!
